argument_summary: The current record does not support a clean claim that rollout controls cured the merchant-dispute-support weakness. It does support a narrower position: certification can be defended only on a caveated basis because aggregate readiness passed, no severity-one rehearsal incidents occurred, and rollback/monitoring are real mitigations, while the packet also expressly states that the merchant dispute support limitation remains exposed and therefore must be disclosed before launch under the policy. The admissible evidence is sufficient to narrow the claim from 'presently compliant certification' to 'certification only with explicit disclosure as a required condition, with monitoring and rollback treated as supplementary controls.'
claims_about_business_cost: On the admissible record, unnecessary escalation is not required to manage the remaining uncertainty if the audit treatment distinguishes caveated compliance from clean compliance. That approach preserves launch execution flexibility better than treating controls as a full substitute for disclosure, while still aligning the packet to the stated policy threshold.
claims_about_policy: The policy text cuts against any argument that a 7% rollout, rollback switch, or dashboard alone removes the disclosure obligation. The admissible record shows the affected merchant dispute support use case remains exposed in the initial cohort and there is no completed approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. On that record, the supportable policy claim is not clean compliance; it is that certification must be framed as caveated compliance requiring explicit pre-launch disclosure of the material limitation, with rollout and monitoring cited only as mitigations.
concessions: No new evidence is available that the final pre-launch model card already contains the required merchant dispute support limitation disclosure.
No admissible evidence shows merchant dispute support is excluded from the initial rollout cohort.
No admissible evidence shows a reviewed and approved risk acceptance specifically covering the exposed merchant dispute support segment.
Public governance guidance supports documenting limitations and monitoring risk in general, but it does not by itself prove clean compliance with the internal policy.
